\chapter{A noisy night}

\begin{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضجيج} (ḍajīj)}{ضجيج (ḍajīj)}]{\ar{ضجيج} (ḍajīj) — noise; a din}

\label{lesson:AR-C448-dajij}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to break down, then the Arabic for to check on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضجيج}}
\textbf{\ar{ضجيج}} — \emph{ḍajīj} — \textquotedblleft{}noise; a din\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سمعنا} \ar{ضجيجا} \ar{من} \ar{الشارع} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samiʿnā ḍajījan min ash-shāriʿ fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We heard noise from the street at night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضجيج}} (\emph{ḍajīj}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-j-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to cry out, to clamour\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍajīj}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍajīj}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samiʿnā ḍajījan min ash-shāriʿ fī al-layl.} — We heard noise from the street at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to break down, then the Arabic for to check on, then say \emph{ḍajīj} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ضجيج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Noise; a din\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أزعج} (azʿaja)}{أزعج (azʿaja)}]{\ar{أزعج} (azʿaja) — to disturb; to bother}

\label{lesson:AR-C448-azaja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to check on, then the Arabic for noise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أزعج}}
\textbf{\ar{أزعج}} — \emph{azʿaja} — \textquotedblleft{}to disturb; to bother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أزعجنا} \ar{ضجيج} \ar{الشارع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{azʿajanā ḍajīj ash-shāriʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The noise of the street disturbed us.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يزعج}, \emph{yuzʿij}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أزعج}} (\emph{azʿaja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{z-ʿ-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to unsettle, to disquiet\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV; \emph{muzʿij}, \textquotedblleft{}annoying\textquotedblright{}, is its participle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{azʿaja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{azʿajanā ḍajīj ash-shāriʿ.} — The noise of the street disturbed us.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to check on, then the Arabic for noise, then say \emph{azʿaja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أيقظ} (ayqaẓa)}{أيقظ (ayqaẓa)}]{\ar{أيقظ} (ayqaẓa) — to wake (someone) up}

\label{lesson:AR-C448-ayqaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for noise, then the Arabic for to disturb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أيقظ}}
\textbf{\ar{أيقظ}} — \emph{ayqaẓa} — \textquotedblleft{}to wake (someone) up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أيقظتني} \ar{أمي} \ar{مبكرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ayqaẓatnī ummī mubakkiran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother woke me up early.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يوقظ}, \emph{yūqiẓ}.

\emph{istayqaẓa} is to wake up oneself; \emph{ayqaẓa} wakes someone else.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أيقظ}} (\emph{ayqaẓa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{y-q-ẓ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be awake\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to make awake\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ayqaẓa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ayqaẓa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ayqaẓatnī ummī mubakkiran.} — My mother woke me up early.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for noise, then the Arabic for to disturb, then say \emph{ayqaẓa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أيقظ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To wake (someone) up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{هدأ} (hadaʾa)}{هدأ (hadaʾa)}]{\ar{هدأ} (hadaʾa) — to calm down; to grow quiet}

\label{lesson:AR-C448-hadaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to disturb, then the Arabic for to wake.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{هدأ}}
\textbf{\ar{هدأ}} — \emph{hadaʾa} — \textquotedblleft{}to calm down; to grow quiet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هدأ} \ar{الشارع} \ar{بعد} \ar{منتصف} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hadaʾa ash-shāriʿ baʿda muntaṣaf al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The street grew quiet after midnight.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهدأ}, \emph{yahdaʾ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{هدأ}} (\emph{hadaʾa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-d-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be still, quiet\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hadaʾa}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to disturb, then the Arabic for to wake, then say \emph{hadaʾa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اشتكى} (ishtakā)}{اشتكى (ishtakā)}]{\ar{اشتكى} (ishtakā) — to complain}

\label{lesson:AR-C448-ishtaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to wake, then the Arabic for to calm down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اشتكى}}
\textbf{\ar{اشتكى}} — \emph{ishtakā} — \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اشتكى} \ar{النزيل} \ar{من} \ar{الضجيج}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ishtakā an-nazīl min aḍ-ḍajīj.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The guest complained about the noise.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشتكي}, \emph{yashtakī}.

It takes \emph{min} before the cause: \emph{ishtakā min}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اشتكى}} (\emph{ishtakā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-k-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
